$comment: How the BDD-only mutation run (stryker.bdd.config.mjs) is split across jobs. One unsharded run mutates every file in src/ against the BDD suite alone and does not finish: its first and only attempt was killed at 30 minutes (nightly-mutation.yml, 2026-09-17), so mutation-bdd-thresholds.json could not be seeded until the sharded run first completed (2026-09-19). Each shard here is a set of directories; nightly-mutation.yml runs one job per shard and merges the reports before the ratchet, so the gate still sees one score per directory.
$invariant: The shards partition src/: every TypeScript file under it belongs to exactly one shard. tests/tdd/mutation-ratchet/bddShards.test.ts fails on a file claimed twice or not at all, so a shard boundary cannot quietly drop a directory from the run. The exclusions in stryker.bdd.config.mjs apply to every shard alike, so the union of the shards mutates exactly what the unsharded glob did.
$balance: Balanced by mutant count, measured with `BDD_MUTATION_SHARD=<name> npx stryker run stryker.bdd.config.mjs --dryRunOnly`. src/core was one shard of 1,545 mutants until 2026-09-18, then three. core-rest was split the same day after a runner reclaimed it at 94% of its 724 mutants, 45 minutes in: src/core/util alone is 324 of them, so core-support (logger and util) and core-root (the remainder of src/core) come out at roughly half each. Shorter shards do not stop a reclaim — nothing inside the job can, the runner goes rather than the process — but they make one cheaper, and the merge refuses an incomplete set by design. nightly-mutation-retry.yml re-runs a reclaimed shard once. Per directory: requestPipeline 503, rateLimiter 401, util 324, pagination 231, circuitBreaker 193, cache 182, logger 63, middleware 35.
